observation.visible_scene: Indoor setting against a plain light wall with a white baseboard and pale wooden floor. On the right edge a long row of small gray dominoes lies flat and undisturbed. In the center-right stands a row of tall vertical domino towers (flat rectangles balanced on edge) colored, left to right, pink, teal, yellow, pink, teal, yellow, pink, teal. To the left of the towers is a heap of scattered multicolored domino pieces (yellow, pink, teal, gray) on the floor.
visible_changes: At the start the leftmost pink tower is already tilted leftward; over t=0.00–0.30s it rotates further left, its top strikes the floor pile, and by t=0.33–0.37s it has collapsed into the heap, with pieces blurring and scattering leftward.

After the pink tower falls, the next teal tower (initially upright) begins tilting left around t=0.47s, leans progressively through t=0.80s, and collapses onto the pile by t=0.93–1.00s, again sending blurred pieces flying left.
The following yellow tower then starts leaning left around t=1.10–1.13s and is still mid-tilt at the last frame (t=1.33s), not yet collapsed.
The four rightmost towers (pink, teal, yellow, pink, teal) remain upright and unchanged throughout the excerpt.
The long gray domino row on the right stays static; the far-left scattered pile stays in place but receives newly flying pieces as each tower collapses.
The wall, baseboard and floor positions are constant across frames, indicating no camera movement.
Motion blur appears on the falling tower segments and on pieces kicked leftward, marking fast motion during each collapse.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the very first leftward tilt of the pink tower (it is already leaning at t=0).
The physical trigger linking each collapsed tower to the next one beginning to tilt (no contact is clearly visible between them).
What happens to the remaining upright towers after the yellow tower finishes falling (clip ends mid-tilt).
The state of the scene before t=0 and after t=1.33s.
uncertain_details: Whether the propagation is a true chain reaction or independent timed releases cannot be determined from these frames.
Exact moment each tower loses contact with its base is approximate due to frame spacing.
Whether any flying pieces land in the far-left pile versus bounce off is not resolvable.
